A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same σ-zero research. Their main text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original attack evaluations on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet, including success rates, perturbation sizes, computational costs, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds target-model comparisons, further budget analyses, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same objective, differentiable ℓ0 approximation, adaptive projection, gradient normalization, and optimization procedure. The added σ-zero* results use different values of existing hyperparameters, without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate sparse, untargeted image-classification attacks on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet. The additional target models and attack budgets change experimental configurations, without adding datasets, domains, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing experiments retain their comparator membership. The added experiments reuse established comparators, including FMN, BBadv, Sparse-RS, and the two Sparse-PGD variants. σ-zero* is a configuration of the proposed attack.

E3.justification: v3 adds two ℓ0-robust CIFAR-10 targets, C11/C12, and two larger ImageNet targets, I7/I8. Table 15 extends white-box iteration budgets from the previous maximum of 5,000 to 10,000 on C3/I2. Tables 6 and 10 additionally evaluate σ=1 and τ0=0.1, alongside the retained defaults. These extend the existing evaluation design.

E4.justification: New Figure 5 examines fixed-budget performance across perturbation budgets on C3 at 1,000 and 5,000 iterations; Table 15 extends the iteration-budget analysis. Tables 6 and 10 add default-versus-adjusted hyperparameter comparisons on C11/C12. Existing hyperparameter ablations remain unchanged, and v2's component ablation is relocated to v3 Table 2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The multiple executions described in v3 Appendix B.3 vary perturbation budgets; they do not establish repeated trials under identical conditions.

E6.justification: v3 substantially expands results with four additional targets, Figure 5, Table 15, and runtime/VRAM entries for fixed-budget comparisons. New Table 6 results expose poor default performance on C11: ASR50 is 15.91%, versus FMN's 74.75%, while the adjusted σ-zero* configuration reaches 85.05%. These are newly reported conditions, not improvements over v2 under matched settings. Most retained scores are unchanged, although Table 13 changes the C7 sPGDp query value from 2.51 to 2.59 thousand.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions, optimization formulation, loss definition, and ℓ0 approximation in Section 2 and Equations 1–7 remain unchanged. No new mathematical results, proofs, or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same methodological contributions and claims about effectiveness, efficiency, reliability, and avoiding costly tuning. Updating the introduction's model count from 18 to 22 expands supporting evidence without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: The explanations of component roles, hyperparameter robustness, and complementary attack behavior remain substantively unchanged. v3 does not add a discussion qualifying these interpretations in light of the poor default results on C11/C12; those differences appear in the reported results.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page public code-repository link, whereas v2 only promises public release upon acceptance. It also specifies the σ-zero* hyperparameters and identifies the additional target models. Existing hardware, batch sizes, and sample counts remain documented as before.

R1.justification: v3 adds Peng et al. (2023) and Mo et al. (2022) as sources for the additional ImageNet targets. The attack taxonomy and novelty positioning remain unchanged. Updating AttackBench from its preprint reference to its publication is bibliographic maintenance.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording and citation-style edits, updates author and publication information, adds acknowledgments, and relocates the Sparse-RS budget explanation. Appendix A.3's redundant discussion disappears after its ablation table moves into the main text; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document template and substantially reorganizes displays: v2 Table 5 becomes main-text Table 2, six groups of minimum-norm curves become two multipanel figures, and fixed-budget tables gain runtime and/or VRAM columns. It also adds Figure 5 and Table 15 and revises captions and table structures. The adversarial-example image panels are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 makes the evaluation more informative through additional target models, budget analyses, fuller computational-cost reporting, and a public code link. Tables 6 and 10 also expose poor default performance on ℓ0-robust models, improving transparency. However, the unchanged claims about shared hyperparameters and consistently superior performance are not reconciled with these results, limiting the overall improvement.
